Timberline Is a Gorgeous Gooseneck Tiny Home With Two Bedrooms, Two Skylights, and a Huge Kitchen
19 photos
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes
Tiny houses are often praised for the way they maximize the use of space through efficient layouts, multifunctional furniture, and other clever design tricks. Gooseneck tiny houses in particular are loved by many because they typically offer more space and comfort than traditional tiny homes on wheels while still remaining highly mobile.
Though they often come with a higher upfront cost than standard bumper-pull tiny homes on wheels, gooseneck models also offer a larger footprint, improved weight distribution, and towing stability. Because they allow for more generous floor plans and can fit more creature comforts, they are preferred by those who want to make as few compromises as possible when moving into a mobile tiny home.
The Timberline by Summit Tiny Homes is a good example of what makes this type of dwelling so appealing. This is a custom-built, two-bedroom tiny house that would suit both couples and families. It features a spacious interior with distinct areas for lounging, cooking, and sleeping, and combines rustic charm with modern amenities. Two skylights, gorgeous live-edge countertops, full-size appliances, and a bathtub are just some of the features that make it stand out from the crowd.
Based in Vernon, British Columbia, Summit Tiny Homes has been part of the tiny living movement since 2017. The company has recently rebranded as Summit Building Co., a move meant to better reflect its expansion beyond tiny homes into custom modular homes, modern cabins, backyard dwellings (ADUs), and bespoke builds, but its focus is still on creating homes that make small-space living a pleasant experience.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes Built on a triple-axle gooseneck trailer, the Timberline measures 42 feet (12.8 meters) in length and 8.6 feet (2.6 meters) in width. Clad in a combination of natural cedar shake shingles and vertical board-and-batten siding, finished in a deep reddish-brown shade, its exterior exudes a rustic vibe that fits perfectly in any natural setting.
The home is topped by a dark, low-profile metal roof, and black-framed windows with reflective glass adorn its facades. Together, these elements give the tiny house a cabin-inspired appearance that feels both traditional and modern.
Characterized by a clutter-free ambiance, the interior is arranged around everyday comfort, ease of movement, and practicality. The layout includes a large U-shaped kitchen, a central living area, a modern bathroom, and two separate sleeping spaces. The raised gooseneck section above the towing vehicle creates an upper zone with ample headroom, perfect for a more comfortable bedroom compared to a traditional loft.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes Accessed via a few wooden stairs, this gooseneck sleeping space is completely private and feels like a proper bedroom. It fits a queen-size bed and a bedside table, as well as a large wardrobe, while two large windows behind and in front of the bed let ample sunlight in.
The second bedroom is located above the kitchen and is accessed by a built-in staircase with integrated storage cabinets. It’s a traditional low-ceiling loft, but offers a comfortable sleeping space that doesn’t take valuable floor space. It fits a queen mattress and is also quite luminous thanks to side windows and a skylight.
Lying under a ceiling with exposed beams, the kitchen is one of the home's standout features. It has a generous U-shaped configuration that provides plenty of room for meal preparation and storage and a charming homestead aesthetic. It features deep forest-green cabinetry complemented by brass hardware, handcrafted live-edge countertops, and a tiled backsplash.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes The countertop extends into a breakfast bar, providing a nice space for casual meals. For modern functionality, the builder equipped the kitchen with a four-burner propane range, an oven, a microwave, a full-size fridge with freezer, and a large sink. A washer/dryer is neatly integrated under the staircase, adding another layer of convenience for full-time living.
The central living room is not very large, but offers a comfortable place to unwind. An L-shaped sectional sofa placed in front of the glass door and a propane fireplace create a cozy atmosphere. As in most tiny houses, the kitchen and living area are connected in a way that encourages easy movement.
Finally, the bathroom inside the Timberline is surprisingly modern and spacious for a tiny house . Instead of a simple shower stall, it has a bathtub and a tiled shower surround, offering a more luxurious experience. The room also includes a vanity with a cute bowl sink, a toilet, and rustic wooden shelves.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes Another thing that makes this home suitable for full-time living is the abundance of storage solutions. Apart from the storage staircase, the kitchen cabinets, and the wardrobe in the main bedroom, there is also a dedicated storage platform above the bathroom, providing plenty of space for personal belongings.
In terms of styling, the interior combines rich wood ceilings, white shiplap walls, and natural timber accents, creating the warm, calming ambiance of a cozy cabin.
Designed to provide year-round comfort, the Timberline features ZIP System R-sheathing, spray-foam insulation, and triple-glazed windows, which help with thermal bridging. A ductless mini-split system provides heating and air conditioning.
The Timberline is a pre-owned tiny house on wheels that’s now waiting for its next owner. The asking price is CAD $225,000 (around USD$157,900).
